audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Jerusalem entry, Zechariah citation, Hosanna, temple action, children praise, fig tree sign, authority dispute, two sons parable, vineyard tenants, cornerstone citation, and kingdom fruit warning.

verses.restored: When they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, toward the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples,

familiar.text: And when they drew nigh unto Jerusalem, and were come to Bethphage, unto the mount of Olives, then sent Jesus two disciples,

modern.text: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two disciples,

original.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤγγισαν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Βηθφαγὴ ⸀εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, τότε ⸀Ἰησοῦς ἀπέστειλεν δύο μαθητὰς

verses.restored: saying to them, Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Loose them and bring them to me.

familiar.text: Saying unto them, Go into the village over against you, and straightway ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them unto me.

modern.text: saying to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and at once you will find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to Me.

original.text: λέγων αὐτοῖς· ⸀Πορεύεσθε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν ⸀κατέναντι ὑμῶν, καὶ ⸀εὐθέως εὑρήσετε ὄνον δεδεμένην καὶ πῶλον μετʼ αὐτῆς· λύσαντες ⸀ἀγάγετέ μοι.

verses.restored: If anyone says anything to you, you shall say, The Lord has need of them, and immediately he will send them.

familiar.text: And if any man say ought unto you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and straightway he will send them.

modern.text: If anyone questions you, tell him that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.”

original.text: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ τι, ἐρεῖτε ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτῶν χρείαν ἔχει· ⸀εὐθὺς δὲ ⸀ἀποστελεῖ αὐτούς.

verses.restored: This happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:

familiar.text: All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying,

modern.text: This took place to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet:

original.text: Τοῦτο ⸀δὲ γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·

verses.restored: Say to daughter Zion: Look, your king comes to you, gentle and mounted on a donkey, and on a colt, offspring of a beast of burden.

familiar.text: Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.

modern.text: “Say to the Daughter of Zion, ‘See, your King comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.’”

original.text: Εἴπατε τῇ θυγατρὶ Σιών· Ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεταί σοι πραῢς καὶ ἐπιβεβηκὼς ἐπὶ ὄνον καὶ ⸀ἐπὶ πῶλον υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου.

verses.restored: The disciples went and did as Jesus instructed them.

familiar.text: And the disciples went, and did as Jesus commanded them,

modern.text: So the disciples went and did as Jesus had directed them.

original.text: πορευθέντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ποιήσαντες καθὼς ⸀συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς

verses.restored: They brought the donkey and the colt, placed garments on them, and he sat upon them.

familiar.text: And brought the ass, and the colt, and put on them their clothes, and they set him thereon.

modern.text: They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.

original.text: ἤγαγον τὴν ὄνον καὶ τὸν πῶλον, καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ⸀ἐπʼ αὐτῶν τὰ ⸀ἱμάτια, καὶ ἐπεκάθισεν ἐπάνω αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: The very great crowd spread their garments on the way; others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the way.

familiar.text: And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way.

modern.text: A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.

original.text: ὁ δὲ πλεῖστος ὄχλος ἔστρωσαν ἑαυτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ἄλλοι δὲ ἔκοπτον κλάδους ἀπὸ τῶν δένδρων καὶ ἐστρώννυον ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.

verses.restored: The crowds going before him and following cried out, Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!

familiar.text: And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.

modern.text: The crowds that went ahead of Him and those that followed were shouting: “Hosanna to the Son of David!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Hosanna in the highest!”

original.text: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι οἱ προάγοντες ⸀αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις.

verses.restored: When he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken, saying, Who is this?

familiar.text: And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this?

modern.text: When Jesus had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and asked, “Who is this?”

original.text: καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐσείσθη πᾶσα ἡ πόλις λέγουσα· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος;

verses.restored: The crowds said, This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.

familiar.text: And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee.

modern.text: The crowds replied, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.” Jesus Cleanses the Temple (Mark 11:15–19; Luke 19:45–48; John 2:12–25)

original.text: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι ἔλεγον· Οὗτός ἐστιν ⸂ὁ προφήτης Ἰησοῦς⸃ ὁ ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲθ τῆς Γαλιλαίας.

verses.restored: Jesus entered the temple and drove out all those buying and selling in the temple; he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling doves.

familiar.text: And Jesus went into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,

modern.text: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and drove out all who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.

original.text: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν ⸀Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ⸀ἱερόν, καὶ ἐξέβαλεν πάντας τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν κατέστρεψεν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστεράς,

verses.restored: He said to them, It has been written, My house will be called a house of prayer, but you are making it a cave of robbers.

familiar.text: And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

modern.text: And He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’ But you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’ ”

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Γέγραπται· Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται, ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ⸀ποιεῖτε σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.

verses.restored: The blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.

familiar.text: And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple; and he healed them.

modern.text: The blind and the lame came to Him at the temple, and He healed them.

original.text: Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ ⸂τυφλοὶ καὶ χωλοὶ⸃ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς.

verses.restored: When the chief priests and scribes saw the wonders he did and the children crying out in the temple, Hosanna to the Son of David, they were indignant.

familiar.text: And when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the son of David; they were sore displeased,

modern.text: But the chief priests and scribes were indignant when they saw the wonders He performed and the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”

original.text: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὰ θαυμάσια ἃ ἐποίησεν καὶ τοὺς παῖδας ⸀τοὺς κράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ λέγοντας· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ, ἠγανάκτησαν

verses.restored: They said to him, Do you hear what these are saying? Jesus said to them, Yes. Have you never read, From the mouth of infants and nursing babies you prepared praise?

familiar.text: And said unto him, Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus saith unto them, Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?

modern.text: “Do you hear what these children are saying?” they asked. “Yes,” Jesus answered. “Have you never read: ‘From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise’ ?”

original.text: καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἀκούεις τί οὗτοι λέγουσιν; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ναί. οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι Ἐκ στόματος νηπίων καὶ θηλαζόντων κατηρτίσω αἶνον;

verses.restored: Leaving them, he went outside the city to Bethany and spent the night there.

familiar.text: And he left them, and went out of the city into Bethany; and he lodged there.

modern.text: Then He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where He spent the night. The Barren Fig Tree (Mark 11:12–14; Mark 11:20–25)

original.text: καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως εἰς Βηθανίαν, καὶ ηὐλίσθη ἐκεῖ.

verses.restored: Early in the morning, returning to the city, he was hungry.

familiar.text: Now in the morning as he returned into the city, he hungered.

modern.text: In the morning, as Jesus was returning to the city, He was hungry.

original.text: ⸀Πρωῒ δὲ ⸀ἐπανάγων εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἐπείνασεν.

verses.restored: Seeing one fig tree by the way, he came to it and found nothing on it except leaves only. He said to it, May fruit never come from you again. And the fig tree withered at once.

familiar.text: And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.

modern.text: Seeing a fig tree by the road, He went up to it but found nothing on it except leaves. “May you never bear fruit again!” He said. And immediately the tree withered.

original.text: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν μίαν ἐπὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ ἦλθεν ἐπʼ αὐτήν, καὶ οὐδὲν εὗρεν ἐν αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ φύλλα μόνον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ· ⸀Μηκέτι ἐκ σοῦ καρπὸς γένηται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· καὶ ἐξηράνθη παραχρῆμα ἡ συκῆ.

verses.restored: When the disciples saw, they marveled, saying, How did the fig tree wither at once?

familiar.text: And when the disciples saw it, they marvelled, saying, How soon is the fig tree withered away!

modern.text: When the disciples saw this, they marveled and asked, “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?”

original.text: καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐθαύμασαν λέγοντες· Πῶς παραχρῆμα ἐξηράνθη ἡ συκῆ;

verses.restored: Jesus answered, Amen, I say to you: if you have trust and do not doubt/divide, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, Be lifted and thrown into the sea, it will happen.

familiar.text: Jesus answered and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do this which is done to the fig tree, but also if ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; it shall be done.

modern.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen.

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν καὶ μὴ διακριθῆτε, οὐ μόνον τὸ τῆς συκῆς ποιήσετε, ἀλλὰ κἂν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ εἴπητε· Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, γενήσεται·

verses.restored: All things, whatever you ask in prayer, trusting, you will receive.

familiar.text: And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.

modern.text: If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.” Jesus’ Authority Challenged (Mark 11:27–33; Luke 20:1–8)

original.text: καὶ πάντα ὅσα ⸀ἂν αἰτήσητε ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ πιστεύοντες λήμψεσθε.

verses.restored: When he entered the temple, the chief priests and elders of the people came to him while he was teaching and said, By what authority do you do these things, and who gave you this authority?

familiar.text: And when he was come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came unto him as he was teaching, and said, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority?

modern.text: When Jesus returned to the temple courts and began to teach, the chief priests and elders of the people came up to Him. “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You this authority?”

original.text: Καὶ ⸂ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ⸃ εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ διδάσκοντι οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ λέγοντες· Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς; καὶ τίς σοι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην;

verses.restored: Jesus answered them, I also will ask you one word; if you tell me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said unto them, I also will ask you one thing, which if ye tell me, I in like wise will tell you by what authority I do these things.

modern.text: “I will also ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον ἕνα, ὃν ἐὰν εἴπητέ μοι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν ἐρῶ ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ·

verses.restored: The baptism of John, from where was it: from heaven or from humans? They reasoned among themselves, saying, If we say, From heaven, he will say to us, Why then did you not trust him?

familiar.text: The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or of men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say unto us, Why did ye not then believe him?

modern.text: What was the source of John’s baptism? Was it from heaven or from men?” They deliberated among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

original.text: τὸ βάπτισμα ⸀τὸ Ἰωάννου πόθεν ἦν; ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων; οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ⸀ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες· Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ ἡμῖν· Διὰ τί οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;

verses.restored: But if we say, From humans, we fear the crowd, for all hold John as a prophet.

familiar.text: But if we shall say, Of men; we fear the people; for all hold John as a prophet.

modern.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we are afraid of the people, for they all regard John as a prophet.”

original.text: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων, φοβούμεθα τὸν ὄχλον, πάντες γὰρ ⸂ὡς προφήτην ἔχουσιν τὸν Ἰωάννην⸃.

verses.restored: They answered Jesus, We do not know. He also said to them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

familiar.text: And they answered Jesus, and said, We cannot tell. And he said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.

modern.text: So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things. The Parable of the Two Sons

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπαν· Οὐκ οἴδαμεν. ἔφη αὐτοῖς καὶ αὐτός· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.

verses.restored: What do you think? A man had two children. Coming to the first, he said, Child, go today and work in the vineyard.

familiar.text: But what think ye? A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard.

modern.text: But what do you think? There was a man who had two sons. He went to the first one and said, ‘Son, go and work today in the vineyard.’

original.text: Τί δὲ ὑμῖν δοκεῖ; ἄνθρωπος εἶχεν τέκνα δύο. ⸀προσελθὼν τῷ πρώτῳ εἶπεν· Τέκνον, ὕπαγε σήμερον ἐργάζου ἐν τῷ ⸀ἀμπελῶνι.

verses.restored: He answered, I will not; but afterward he regretted it and went.

familiar.text: He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went.

modern.text: ‘I will not,’ he replied. But later he changed his mind and went.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· ⸂Οὐ θέλω· ὕστερον δὲ μεταμεληθεὶς⸃ ἀπῆλθεν.

verses.restored: Coming to the other, he said the same. He answered, I go, lord, but did not go.

familiar.text: And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.

modern.text: Then the man went to the second son and told him the same thing. ‘I will, sir,’ he said. But he did not go.

original.text: ⸂προσελθὼν δὲ⸃ τῷ ⸀δευτέρῳ εἶπεν ὡσαύτως· ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· ⸂Ἐγώ, κύριε· καὶ οὐκ⸃ ἀπῆλθεν.

verses.restored: Which of the two did the will of the father? They said, The first. Jesus said to them, Amen, I say to you: tax collectors and prostitutes are going before you into the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: Whether of them twain did the will of his father? They say unto him, The first. Jesus saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.

modern.text: Which of the two did the will of his father?” “The first, ” they answered. Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God before you.

original.text: τίς ἐκ τῶν δύο ἐποίησεν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός; ⸀λέγουσιν· Ὁ ⸀πρῶτος. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οἱ τελῶναι καὶ αἱ πόρναι προάγουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: For John came to you in the way of righteousness/justice, and you did not trust him; but tax collectors and prostitutes trusted him. You, seeing this, did not afterward regret/turn so as to trust him.

familiar.text: For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.

modern.text: For John came to you in a righteous way and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and prostitutes did. And even after you saw this, you did not repent and believe him. The Parable of the Wicked Tenants (Mark 12:1–12; Luke 20:9–18)

original.text: ἦλθεν γὰρ ⸂Ἰωάννης πρὸς ὑμᾶς⸃ ἐν ὁδῷ δικαιοσύνης, καὶ οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ· οἱ δὲ τελῶναι καὶ αἱ πόρναι ἐπίστευσαν αὐτῷ· ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰδόντες ⸀οὐδὲ μετεμελήθητε ὕστερον τοῦ πιστεῦσαι αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Hear another parable. There was a householder who planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it, built a tower, leased it to farmers, and went away.

familiar.text: Hear another parable: There was a certain householder, which planted a vineyard, and hedged it round about, and digged a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country:

modern.text: Listen to another parable: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

original.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἀκούσατε. ⸀Ἄνθρωπος ἦν οἰκοδεσπότης ὅστις ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα καὶ φραγμὸν αὐτῷ περιέθηκεν καὶ ὤρυξεν ἐν αὐτῷ ληνὸν καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν.

verses.restored: When the season of fruits drew near, he sent his servants to the farmers to receive his fruits.

familiar.text: And when the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, that they might receive the fruits of it.

modern.text: When the harvest time drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit.

original.text: ὅτε δὲ ἤγγισεν ὁ καιρὸς τῶν καρπῶν, ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς λαβεῖν τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: The farmers took his servants; one they beat, another they killed, another they stoned.

familiar.text: And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.

modern.text: But the tenants seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.

original.text: καὶ λαβόντες οἱ γεωργοὶ τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὃν μὲν ἔδειραν, ὃν δὲ ἀπέκτειναν, ὃν δὲ ἐλιθοβόλησαν.

verses.restored: Again he sent other servants, more than the first; they did the same to them.

familiar.text: Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they did unto them likewise.

modern.text: Again, he sent other servants, more than the first group. But the tenants did the same to them.

original.text: πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους πλείονας τῶν πρώτων, καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτοῖς ὡσαύτως.

verses.restored: Finally he sent his son to them, saying, They will respect my son.

familiar.text: But last of all he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son.

modern.text: Finally, he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.

original.text: ὕστερον δὲ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου.

verses.restored: But the farmers, seeing the son, said among themselves, This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and have his inheritance.

familiar.text: But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance.

modern.text: But when the tenants saw the son, they said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’

original.text: οἱ δὲ γεωργοὶ ἰδόντες τὸν υἱὸν εἶπον ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτὸν καὶ ⸀σχῶμεν τὴν κληρονομίαν αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: Taking him, they threw him outside the vineyard and killed him.

familiar.text: And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.

modern.text: So they seized him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.

original.text: καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἐξέβαλον ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος καὶ ἀπέκτειναν.

verses.restored: Therefore when the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?

familiar.text: When the lord therefore of the vineyard cometh, what will he do unto those husbandmen?

modern.text: Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard returns, what will he do to those tenants?”

original.text: ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος, τί ποιήσει τοῖς γεωργοῖς ἐκείνοις;

verses.restored: They said to him, He will bring those harmful ones to a harmful end and lease the vineyard to other farmers who will give him the fruits in their seasons.

familiar.text: They say unto him, He will miserably destroy those wicked men, and will let out his vineyard unto other husbandmen, which shall render him the fruits in their seasons.

modern.text: “He will bring those wretches to a wretched end,” they replied, “and will rent out the vineyard to other tenants who will give him his share of the fruit at harvest time.”

original.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κακοὺς κακῶς ἀπολέσει αὐτούς, καὶ τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἐκδώσεται ἄλλοις γεωργοῖς, οἵτινες ἀποδώσουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς καρποὺς ἐν τοῖς καιροῖς αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, Have you never read in the Scriptures: The stone the builders rejected, this became the head of the corner; from the Lord this came to be, and it is marvelous in our eyes?

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?

modern.text: Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’ ?

original.text: Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας· παρὰ κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη, καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν;

verses.restored: Therefore I say to you: the reign of the Divine will be taken from you and given to a people producing its fruits.

familiar.text: Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.

modern.text: Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.

original.text: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἀρθήσεται ἀφʼ ὑμῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ δοθήσεται ἔθνει ποιοῦντι τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: The one falling on this stone will be broken; on whomever it falls, it will scatter him like chaff.

familiar.text: And whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.

modern.text: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed. ”

original.text: ⸂Καὶ ὁ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὸν λίθον τοῦτον συνθλασθήσεται· ἐφʼ ὃν δʼ ἂν πέσῃ λικμήσει αὐτόν.⸃

verses.restored: When the chief priests and Pharisees heard his parables, they knew he was speaking about them.

familiar.text: And when the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they perceived that he spake of them.

modern.text: When the chief priests and Pharisees heard His parables, they knew that Jesus was speaking about them.

original.text: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὰς παραβολὰς αὐτοῦ ἔγνωσαν ὅτι περὶ αὐτῶν λέγει·

verses.restored: Though they sought to seize him, they feared the crowds, because they held him as a prophet.

familiar.text: But when they sought to lay hands on him, they feared the multitude, because they took him for a prophet.

modern.text: Although they wanted to arrest Him, they were afraid of the crowds, because the people regarded Him as a prophet.

original.text: καὶ ζητοῦντες αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι ἐφοβήθησαν τοὺς ὄχλους, ⸂ἐπεὶ εἰς⸃ προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον.
